content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I would like to know if I can use my 16VDC motion sensor as an input for my [product_name] [product_name] model. Please refer to the attached specifications for the motion sensor and wiring details. See attachment 1 & 2. Much appreciated. [user_name]

No, that's not possible. For a 16VDC sensor, you would need a [product_name] that supports 12/24V. The [product_name] [product_name] model requires more than 79V AC/DC to detect a signal at its inputs. This information is available in the technical data section of the manual.
Is it possible to use a 16VDC relay to convert the signal to a 120V/230V input for the [product_name]? [user_name]
Hello! The relay's coil voltage isn’t relevant to the [product_name]; what matters is the voltage supplied to the [product_name] input.

I understand. My suggestion is to place the relay between the motion sensor output and the [product_name] input. The [product_name] requires a 120/230V signal, so you can use the motion sensor’s 16VDC output to power a relay coil, which then switches a 120/230VAC signal to the [product_name]. Each component must have its required voltage supplied. When the sensor detects motion, it should close a contact, correct?

Often, relays are used on the output side, and your approach should work. Here are some considerations: 1) If you use the 16VDC output from the motion sensor to close a relay coil, ensure the sensor has enough power to trigger it. 2) The transition from the sensor to the relay needs to be fast and clean to prevent the relay from 'bouncing' or 'chattering'—check both device specifications. 3) The relay should be powered with the same AC supply as the [product_name], ideally on the same phase. 4) A smaller relay is preferable; you only need enough voltage for the [product_name] to recognize the signal, and the coil doesn't need much power if the sensor output is sufficient. 5) Consider how quickly the sensor output changes, as this impacts relay durability over many cycles. 6) Adding a relay between sensor and control device introduces a minor delay, but it shouldn't affect this application. Good luck with your project!

The moderator separated my answer into a new thread. See my post titled, "Is it possible to use a 16VDC relay to convert the signal to a 120V/230V input for the [product_name]?" You can achieve your goal; it just requires a few extra components.
Hello [user_name], apologies for the mistake. I've now moved the posts back into this discussion. Kind regards, [user_name]
No worries. I probably shouldn’t have replied with another question.
